alternatives: Content-level dedup: suppress a second identical text within a time window — considered and rejected, because an admin who sends the same announcement twice intends two sends.
Make the broadcast enqueue reuse an existing queued row when the text matches — rejected, it would merge two deliberate admin actions into one.
extracted_decision.rationale: Measured: identical text enqueued twice produced two Broadcast rows, 12 message rows (2 per recipient) and 2 device pushes; two distinct texts produced exactly 6 messages and 6 PushOutbox keys each with zero duplication. Dedup keys on the broadcast identity (push key message_broadcast_<broadcastId>_<uid>, message ids buildNestedObjectId('users', uid, 'messages', broadcastId)). The Manager confirmed the reworded M35 S6 clause and declined content-level dedup.
extracted_decision.summary: Broadcast dedup keys on the broadcast identity, not on the message text. Two separate submissions of the same text are two broadcasts and must each deliver; no content-level dedup is to be built.
extracted_decision.tradeoffs: Simple, predictable admin semantics plus an idempotent worker retry, at the cost of a duplicate-send footgun if an admin submits the same announcement twice by accident.
